content.description: A Frontend Developer builds the user-facing part of websites and web applications — the layout, visual design, and interactivity that users see and click on directly in their browser. They translate UI/UX designs into working code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, and a framework such as React, Vue, or Angular), consume the APIs that Backend Developers expose, and are responsible for performance, responsiveness across devices, and cross-browser compatibility. Unlike a Backend Developer, who focuses on server logic, databases, and APIs that users never see, a Frontend Developer owns everything rendered in the browser. Unlike a Full-stack Developer, who splits attention across both layers, a dedicated Frontend Developer typically goes deeper on UI architecture, client-side performance, and design-system implementation.

vnMarket.value: Frontend là một trong những vị trí kỹ thuật lõi được doanh nghiệp CNTT tại Việt Nam ưu tiên tuyển dụng nhiều nhất: theo Báo cáo Thị trường Tuyển dụng thường niên 2025-2026 của TopCV, Lập trình viên Web (nhóm Frontend) là vị trí được doanh nghiệp IT ưu tiên tuyển dụng nhiều nhất, chiếm 45% nhu cầu tuyển lập trình viên, trong khi ngành IT - Phần mềm nói chung thuộc top 2 nhóm ngành có nhu cầu tuyển dụng lớn nhất trong giai đoạn tới.

salary.value: Mức lương trung vị của Frontend Developer tại Việt Nam là khoảng 34,8 triệu VNĐ/tháng theo khảo sát chung; chia theo kinh nghiệm: ~30,8 triệu (3-4 năm), ~41,8 triệu (5-8 năm), ~46,3 triệu (trên 8 năm) — theo ITviec IT Salary & Recruitment Market Report 2025-2026 (khảo sát 1.839 người).

demand.value: Frontend Developer đứng thứ 3 trong top các vị trí IT được săn đón nhất tại Việt Nam trong 6 tháng đầu năm 2025, theo ITviec Blog.

similarJobs.name: Backend Developer
similarJobs.distinction: Builds server-side logic, APIs, and databases that run behind the scenes, rather than the visual interface and client-side code users interact with directly.

similarJobs.name: Full-stack Developer
similarJobs.distinction: Works across both frontend and backend layers, trading depth in UI architecture and client-side performance for broader end-to-end coverage of a feature.

similarJobs.name: UI/UX Designer
similarJobs.distinction: Designs wireframes, visual mockups, and interaction flows in design tools; does not write the production code that renders them in a browser.

similarJobs.name: Mobile Developer (iOS/Android)
similarJobs.distinction: Builds native or cross-platform mobile app interfaces (Swift/Kotlin/Flutter/React Native) rather than browser-based web interfaces.

hardSkills.name: HTML & CSS
hardSkills.description: The foundational languages for structuring content and styling every web interface a Frontend Developer ships.

hardSkills.name: JavaScript & TypeScript
hardSkills.description: JavaScript powers all client-side interactivity; TypeScript adds static typing that Vietnamese product teams increasingly require for maintainability at scale.

hardSkills.name: Modern frontend framework (React, Vue, or Angular)
hardSkills.description: Most production Vietnamese web products are built on a component-based framework rather than plain JavaScript, so fluency in at least one is a baseline hiring requirement.

hardSkills.name: Responsive & cross-browser design
hardSkills.description: Interfaces must render correctly across phones, tablets, desktops, and different browsers — a constant practical constraint in frontend work.

hardSkills.name: API integration (REST/GraphQL)
hardSkills.description: Frontend code consumes backend-provided APIs to fetch and submit data, so understanding request/response contracts is essential.

hardSkills.name: Version control (Git)
hardSkills.description: Nearly all frontend teams collaborate through Git-based workflows, branching, and code review.

hardSkills.name: Build tooling & performance optimization (Webpack/Vite, bundling, lazy-loading)
hardSkills.description: Shipping fast-loading pages requires understanding how code is bundled, minified, and split for delivery.

softSkills.name: Attention to detail
softSkills.description: Pixel-level UI discrepancies and small interaction bugs are highly visible to end users, so precision matters more than in many other engineering roles.

softSkills.name: Cross-functional communication
softSkills.description: Frontend Developers coordinate constantly with designers (on feasibility/handoff) and backend engineers (on API contracts).

softSkills.name: Problem-solving / debugging
softSkills.description: Diagnosing rendering issues, state bugs, and browser-specific quirks is a daily part of the job.

softSkills.name: Adaptability
softSkills.description: Frontend frameworks, tooling, and best practices evolve quickly, so staying current with new patterns is expected.

softSkills.name: Time management
softSkills.description: Frontend work is often on the critical path just before a release/demo, requiring reliable estimation and delivery.
